topics.title: Propositional Logic
topics.definition: Propositional logic studies statements that are either true or false and how they combine.

children.title: Propositions and truth values
children.definition: A proposition is a declarative statement with a definite truth value, such as "2 + 2 = 4".

children.title: Logical connectives
children.definition: Negation, conjunction, disjunction, exclusive or, implication and biconditional.

children.title: Truth tables
children.definition: A table listing the truth value of a compound statement for every combination of its variables.

children.title: Tautology, contradiction and contingency
children.definition: Always true, always false and sometimes true statements respectively.

children.title: Logical equivalence and laws
children.definition: Identity, domination, idempotent, double negation, commutative, associative, distributive, De Morgan and absorption laws.

children.title: Normal forms
children.definition: Conjunctive and disjunctive normal forms, and functional completeness of the connectives.

children.title: Arguments and validity
children.definition: An argument is valid when the conclusion must be true whenever all premises are true.

topics.title: Predicates and Quantifiers
topics.definition: Predicate logic extends propositional logic with variables, predicates and quantifiers.

children.title: Predicates
children.definition: A statement involving variables, such as P(x) meaning x is greater than 3, which becomes a proposition when x is fixed.

children.title: Universal quantifier
children.definition: For all x, written with an upside down A, true when P(x) holds for every element of the domain.

children.title: Existential quantifier
children.definition: There exists an x, written with a backwards E, true when at least one element satisfies P(x).

children.title: Negating quantified statements
children.definition: The negation of for all is there exists a counterexample, and the negation of there exists is for all not.

children.title: Nested quantifiers
children.definition: Statements such as for all x there exists y, where the order of quantifiers changes the meaning.

children.title: Rules of inference
children.definition: Modus ponens, modus tollens, hypothetical syllogism, disjunctive syllogism, addition, simplification, conjunction and resolution.

children.title: Fallacies
children.definition: The fallacy of affirming the consequent and of denying the antecedent, which look valid but are not.

topics.title: Methods of Proof
topics.definition: A proof is a valid argument that establishes the truth of a mathematical statement.

children.title: Direct proof
children.definition: Assume the hypothesis and derive the conclusion by known facts and algebra.

children.title: Indirect proof by contraposition
children.definition: Prove the contrapositive, that not q implies not p, which is logically equivalent to p implies q.

children.title: Proof by contradiction
children.definition: Assume the statement is false and derive a contradiction, used classically to prove the irrationality of the square root of 2.

children.title: Vacuous and trivial proof
children.definition: A conditional is vacuously true when the hypothesis is false and trivially true when the conclusion is known to be true.

children.title: Proof by cases and exhaustive proof
children.definition: Split the statement into covering cases and prove each one.

children.title: Existence and uniqueness proofs
children.definition: Show that an object exists, and if required that it is the only one.

children.title: Constructive versus non constructive proof
children.definition: Either produce the object or prove it must exist without producing it.

topics.title: Proof Strategies and Mathematical Induction
topics.definition: Strategies guide which proof method to try, and induction proves statements about all natural numbers.

children.title: Forward and backward reasoning
children.definition: Work from the hypothesis towards the goal, or from the goal backwards to known facts.

children.title: Adapting an existing proof and looking for counterexamples
children.definition: Reuse known proofs with modifications, and test small cases before attempting a proof.

children.title: Principle of mathematical induction
children.definition: Prove the base case and the inductive step that P(k) implies P(k + 1), which proves P(n) for all n.

children.title: Strong induction and well ordering
children.definition: Strong induction assumes all smaller cases, and the well ordering property says every non-empty set of positive integers has a least element.

children.title: Common induction mistakes
children.definition: Assuming what is to be proved and skipping the base case.

topics.title: Sets
topics.definition: A set is an unordered collection of distinct objects called its elements.

children.title: Set builder and roster notation
children.definition: Sets are listed as {1, 2, 3} or described as {x | x is an even integer}.

children.title: Subsets and power set
children.definition: A is a subset of B if every element of A is in B; the power set is the set of all subsets and has 2 to the n elements.

children.title: Set operations
children.definition: Union, intersection, difference, complement and symmetric difference.

children.title: Set identities and Venn diagrams
children.definition: Algebraic identities such as De Morgan laws together with diagrams that show operations visually.

children.title: Cardinality and inclusion exclusion
children.definition: The size of a set, with the two set rule |A union B| = |A| + |B| - |A intersection B|.

children.title: Cartesian product and ordered pairs
children.definition: The set of all ordered pairs from two sets, which underlies relations and functions.

topics.title: Functions
topics.definition: A function maps each element of its domain to exactly one element of its codomain.

children.title: Domain, codomain and range
children.definition: The allowed inputs, the declared output set and the outputs actually produced.

children.title: Injective (one to one) function
children.definition: Different inputs always give different outputs.

children.title: Surjective (onto) function
children.definition: Every element of the codomain is the image of some input.

children.title: Bijective function and inverse
children.definition: Both injective and surjective, so an inverse function exists.

children.title: Composition and graphs of functions
children.definition: Composition applies one function after another, and the graph shows the ordered pairs.

children.title: Important functions
children.definition: Identity, constant, floor, ceiling, factorial and exponential functions.

topics.title: Sequences and Sums
topics.definition: A sequence is an ordered list of numbers and a sum adds the terms of a sequence.

children.title: Arithmetic progression
children.definition: Each term differs from the previous one by a constant, with sum n over 2 times first plus last.

children.title: Geometric progression
children.definition: Each term is a constant multiple of the previous one, with sum a(r to the n minus 1) over (r minus 1).

children.title: Recurrence relations
children.definition: A sequence defined by earlier terms, such as the Fibonacci relation.

children.title: Special integer sequences
children.definition: Fibonacci numbers, factorials, powers and triangular numbers.

children.title: Summation notation and formulas
children.definition: Sigma notation, sums of constants, arithmetic series, geometric series and sums of squares and cubes.

topics.title: Matrices
topics.definition: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers used to represent data and transformations.

children.title: Matrix types
children.definition: Row, column, square, diagonal, identity, symmetric and zero matrices.

children.title: Matrix operations
children.definition: Addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication and matrix multiplication with its row by column rule.

children.title: Transpose and trace
children.definition: The transpose swaps rows and columns and the trace adds the diagonal elements.

children.title: Inverse of a matrix
children.definition: Exists only for square matrices with non-zero determinant, with A times inverse equals identity.

children.title: Boolean matrices
children.definition: Entries are 0 and 1 with the join and meet operations, used to represent relations.

topics.title: Relations
topics.definition: A relation from A to B is a subset of the Cartesian product A cross B.

children.title: Binary relations and their representation
children.definition: Sets of ordered pairs shown as lists, matrices or directed graphs.

children.title: Properties of relations
children.definition: Reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric, transitive and irreflexive on a set.

children.title: Equivalence relations
children.definition: Reflexive, symmetric and transitive; they partition the set into equivalence classes.

children.title: Partial ordering relations
children.definition: Reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive; Hasse diagrams draw them compactly, with maximal, minimal, least and greatest elements.

children.title: Closures of relations
children.definition: The reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure, with Warshall algorithm for transitive closure.

children.title: n-ary relations and databases
children.definition: Relations of degree n as tables, with primary keys as candidate keys and operations like selection and projection.

topics.title: Divisibility and Modular Arithmetic
topics.definition: Divisibility studies when one integer divides another exactly, and modular arithmetic keeps only remainders.

children.title: Division algorithm and divisibility
children.definition: For integers a and d with d positive there are unique q and r with a = dq + r and 0 <= r < d; d divides a if r is 0.

children.title: Congruence modulo m
children.definition: a is congruent to b mod m when m divides a minus b, which means both leave the same remainder.

children.title: Arithmetic modulo m
children.definition: Addition and multiplication wrap around using the remainder, which models clocks and hashing.

children.title: Applications of modular arithmetic
children.definition: Hash functions, check digits, day of the week arithmetic and cryptography.

children.title: Linear congruences
children.definition: Equations ax congruent to b mod m, solvable when the gcd of a and m divides b.

topics.title: Integer Algorithms
topics.definition: Classical algorithms work on integers and many of them run in time proportional to the number of digits.

children.title: Integer representation and base conversion
children.definition: Numbers in base b are converted to decimal by expansion and back by repeated division.

children.title: Euclidean algorithm for GCD
children.definition: Repeatedly replace the pair by the divisor and remainder until the remainder is zero.

children.title: Extended Euclidean algorithm
children.definition: Also finds the coefficients x and y such that ax + by equals the gcd, which gives modular inverses.

children.title: Finding modular inverses
children.definition: The inverse of a modulo m exists when gcd is 1 and is found by the extended Euclidean algorithm.

children.title: Complexity of integer algorithms
children.definition: Bit operations count for addition, multiplication and division, and the running times of gcd computations.

children.title: Linear Diophantine equations
children.definition: Equations of the form ax + by = c are solvable exactly when gcd divides c.

topics.title: Primes and Greatest Common Divisor
topics.definition: A prime has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself, and the gcd is the largest common divisor.

children.title: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic
children.definition: Every integer greater than 1 factors uniquely into primes up to order.

children.title: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic applications
children.definition: Finding gcd and lcm from prime factorisations.

children.title: Relatively prime numbers
children.definition: Two integers whose gcd is 1; pairwise relatively prime sets are used in number theory and cryptography.

children.title: Least common multiple
children.definition: The smallest positive integer divisible by both numbers, equal to a times b divided by gcd.

children.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes and trial division
children.definition: Methods for listing or testing primes; trial division needs checking divisors up to the square root.

children.title: Mersenne and Fermat primes
children.definition: Primes of the form 2 to the p minus 1 and Fermat numbers, with a role in primality testing.

topics.title: Congruences and Classical Theorems
topics.definition: Congruence equations and famous theorems make computation with large numbers practical.

children.title: Systems of linear congruences
children.definition: Solved by substitution or by the Chinese remainder theorem.

children.title: Chinese remainder theorem
children.definition: A system of congruences with pairwise relatively prime moduli has a unique solution modulo their product.

children.title: Fermat little theorem
children.definition: If p is prime and a is not divisible by p then a to the p minus 1 is congruent to 1 mod p.

children.title: Euler theorem and totient
children.definition: Generalises Fermat with the totient phi, which counts integers up to n that are coprime to n.

children.title: Applications to cryptography
children.definition: RSA uses modular exponentiation, the totient function and large primes for public key encryption.

topics.title: Groups
topics.definition: A group is a set with one binary operation that is associative, has an identity and gives every element an inverse.

children.title: Definition and axioms
children.definition: Closure, associativity, identity element and inverse element define a group.

children.title: Abelian group
children.definition: A group in which the operation is also commutative.

children.title: Examples of groups
children.definition: Integers under addition, non-zero rationals under multiplication and symmetries of a figure under composition.

children.title: Order of a group and of an element
children.definition: The number of elements in the group, and the smallest positive n with a to the n equal to the identity.

children.title: Subgroups
children.definition: A subset that is itself a group under the same operation, tested by closure and inverse conditions.

children.title: Permutation groups and symmetries
children.definition: Groups whose elements are bijections of a set, and the dihedral groups of polygons.

topics.title: Cyclic Groups and Homomorphism
topics.definition: A cyclic group is generated by one element, and a homomorphism is a structure preserving map between groups.

children.title: Cyclic group
children.definition: Every element is a power of a single generator g, such as the integers under addition with generator 1.

children.title: Generators and order
children.definition: The order of a cyclic group equals the order of its generator, and subgroups of cyclic groups are cyclic.

children.title: Group homomorphism
children.definition: A map f with f of a times b equal to f of a times f of b, preserving the operation.

children.title: Kernel and image
children.definition: The set mapping to the identity and the set of all images, both of which are subgroups.

children.title: Isomorphism
children.definition: A bijective homomorphism, which means the two groups are structurally the same.

children.title: Properties of homomorphisms
children.definition: Order preservation, the kernel as a normal subgroup and the first isomorphism theorem.

topics.title: Cosets, Normal Subgroups and Lagrange Theorem
topics.definition: Cosets split a group into equal sized blocks, and Lagrange theorem relates their size to the group order.

children.title: Left and right cosets
children.definition: Sets aH or Ha formed by multiplying a fixed element with every element of a subgroup.

children.title: Coset properties
children.definition: Cosets of a subgroup partition the group and all have the same size as the subgroup.

children.title: Index of a subgroup
children.definition: The number of distinct cosets, equal to the order of the group divided by the order of the subgroup.

children.title: Lagrange theorem
children.definition: The order of a subgroup divides the order of the finite group, so the order of every element divides the group order.

children.title: Normal subgroup
children.definition: A subgroup with aH equal to Ha for every a, which is exactly what allows a quotient group to be formed.

children.title: Quotient group and simple groups
children.definition: A quotient group is formed from the cosets of a normal subgroup; simple groups have no proper non-trivial normal subgroup.

topics.title: Rings and Fields
topics.definition: A ring has two operations with addition forming a group and multiplication distributing over it, and a field adds division.

children.title: Ring definition
children.definition: An abelian group under addition with an associative multiplication that distributes over addition.

children.title: Commutative ring and unity
children.definition: A ring where multiplication is commutative, with or without a multiplicative identity element.

children.title: Integral domain
children.definition: A commutative ring with unity and no zero divisors, so cancellation works.

children.title: Field definition and examples
children.definition: A commutative ring with unity in which every non-zero element has an inverse; rationals, reals and integers modulo a prime are fields.

children.title: Characteristic of a ring
children.definition: The smallest positive n with n times 1 equal to 0, which is 0, a prime or a composite.

children.title: Polynomial rings and applications
children.definition: Rings of polynomials and their use in coding theory and cryptography; finite fields underlie AES and error correcting codes.

topics.title: Basics of Counting
topics.definition: Counting determines the size of a set without listing all its elements.

children.title: Product rule
children.definition: If one task has m outcomes and a second has n, the pair has m times n outcomes.

children.title: Sum rule
children.definition: If two cases cannot happen together with m and n outcomes, the total is m + n.

children.title: Subtraction (inclusion exclusion) rule
children.definition: For overlapping cases, the total is m + n minus the number of common outcomes.

children.title: Tree diagrams
children.definition: A branching diagram that shows all outcomes of a sequence of choices.

children.title: Counting with sets and functions
children.definition: Counting subsets, functions between finite sets and the number of injective functions.

topics.title: Pigeonhole Principle
topics.definition: If more items than boxes are placed into boxes, some box holds more than one item.

children.title: Simple pigeonhole principle
children.definition: Placing n + 1 objects into n boxes forces at least one box to hold two objects.

children.title: Generalised pigeonhole principle
children.definition: Placing N objects into k boxes forces some box to hold at least the ceiling of N divided by k objects.

children.title: Classical applications
children.definition: Among any 13 people two share a birth month, and among n + 1 integers chosen from 1 to 2n one divides another.

children.title: Subsequence and geometry applications
children.definition: Any sequence of n squared + 1 distinct numbers has an increasing or decreasing subsequence of length n + 1.

topics.title: Permutations and Combinations
topics.definition: A permutation counts ordered arrangements and a combination counts unordered selections.

children.title: Permutations without repetition
children.definition: The number of ways to arrange r items chosen from n is n factorial divided by (n minus r) factorial.

children.title: Permutations with repetition
children.definition: Arrangements when items may repeat are n to the power r.

children.title: Circular permutations
children.definition: Arrangements around a circle number (n minus 1) factorial because rotations are the same.

children.title: Combinations
children.definition: The number of r element subsets of an n element set is n factorial over r factorial times (n minus r) factorial.

children.title: Combinations with repetition
children.definition: Distributions of identical objects into distinct boxes number C of (n plus r minus 1) choose r.

children.title: Permutations and combinations with restrictions
children.definition: Cases with adjacent items, no two together, or fixed positions handled by first arranging the restricted items.

topics.title: Binomial Coefficients and the Binomial Theorem
topics.definition: Binomial coefficients count selections and appear as the coefficients in the expansion of a power of a binomial.

children.title: Binomial theorem
children.definition: The expansion of (x plus y) to the n as a sum of C(n, k) times x to the n minus k times y to the k.

children.title: Pascal triangle and Pascal identity
children.definition: Each entry is the sum of the two above it, which is the identity C(n, k) = C(n-1, k-1) + C(n-1, k).

children.title: Useful identities
children.definition: C(n, k) = C(n, n-k), the sum of all C(n, k) is 2 to the n, and Vandermonde identity.

children.title: Multinomial coefficients and theorem
children.definition: Counting arrangements of objects of several types, and the expansion of a sum of several terms.

children.title: Applications of counting
children.definition: Probability of card and dice outcomes, password strength, seat allocation and algorithm analysis.
